lines.en: Before long, the plain was torn apart and stained with the blood of battle.
No, it could no longer be called a battle.
Entrails spilled from the waists of small people torn in two. With every step the Japanese took, the small people's bodies were trampled and burst like swollen, soggy noodles.
“Aaaaaah······.”
“S-spare me! Please, spare me!”
Even those tiny screams carried the same weight of life.
They were only smaller in size. They, too, were humans who must have led ordinary lives, just like the people of Earth, until the scenarios descended.
People who must have eaten, worked, and lived ordinary lives with their families······.
Familiar scenes from Earth overlapped with the fallen bodies of the small people.
The Japanese shouted.
“Hahaha! So this is what it felt like!”
Perhaps Xunzi should have been born in this age.
Evidence for his doctrine that human nature was evil lay everywhere.
This was a world where even victims who had been slaughtered by others moments earlier could turn into perpetrators at once, as long as they were given power and a system of rewards.
Perhaps all the more so because they had suffered it themselves.
Shin Yoosung asked through gritted teeth.
“······How can they do that?”
She probably wasn't asking because she genuinely wanted to know.
Because we already knew the answer.
Without a word, I placed a hand on Shin Yoosung's shoulder.
Her shoulders trembled as if she were carrying a heavy burden.
“That's going too far······!”
Getting coins, getting new items, getting skills, and growing stronger.
Everyone knew that was the only way to survive even a little longer in this world.
That was why every survivor understood the other survivors.
And that was why some survivors had to live ashamed of the fact that they understood.
“O d-disaster······.”
Inching along, a small person whose lower body had been torn away crawled toward our feet.
“P-please, have mercy······.”
Power beyond all reason inspired awe as well as fear.
To the inhabitants of Peace Land, Earthlings were probably gods as well as disasters.
I bent down and held out a finger to the small person approaching me.
The small person reached for that finger. Amid the sound of ragged breaths, a tiny touch met my fingertip.
At the moment of that final breath, a strange joy suffused the small person's face. As if they had touched a god, as if that alone had granted salvation.
[Carry out your duties as a disaster.]
And we were supposed to kill these tiny people.
Right beside me, I felt Shin Yoosung's presence as she radiated blazing magic power.
I worried she might charge straight at the Japanese, but unexpectedly, her killing intent pointed in a very reasonable direction.
“All of this······ is another scenario those bastards made, isn't it?”
An intermediate dokkaebi.
Unlike the other low-ranking dokkaebis, a good-looking dokkaebi floated in the air, arms casually folded.
It wasn't Paul, who had been dragged off to the Bureau. His body was probably melting away in the Hell of Scorching Heat by now.
I recalled the passage from ‘Ways of Survival’ that I had read beforehand.
「The intermediate dokkaebi overseeing the ‘Abandoned World’ scenario. Its name was ‘Ganul.’」
The intermediate dokkaebi Ganul spoke.
[As expected, the third wave of participants from the ‘Japan Dome’ is off to a fiery start. I hope you all earn plenty of coins here in ‘Peace Land’ and then return.]
The third wave already······.
As expected, those in the ‘Japan Dome’ seemed to be progressing through the scenarios at a tremendous pace.
“Haha, this is fantastic! No wonder the first- and second-wave guys practically jizzed themselves rushing over here!”
“Did you see those coins come in? This scenario's a total freebie!”
[Many constellations are excited.]
[Some constellations wish to see ten small people trampled to death at once.]
Shin Yoosung's briefly stunned expression soon filled with rage.
“It's because of those bastards······!”
But that rage had nowhere to go.
The constellations were beings at the very top of the <Star Stream>.
They were beyond the reach of Shin Yoosung, who was merely an ‘incarnation’ within the scenarios.
That was why all we could do now was find a scapegoat before us to bear the brunt of our rage.
“Hahaha, ten at once! I'll kill them first!”
There was no longer any trace of reason in the eyes of the Japanese swinging their katanas in ecstasy.
To them, the small people probably looked like living coins.
“Ajusshi, over there······!”
That was when a small person clad in heavy armor stepped out from among the others.
The small person seemed to be their commander.
“Glory to Kal—Savior!”
The small commander raised a longsword with all their might, then bravely charged at the disaster. The Japanese man swung his katana as if swatting a nuisance.
Whooosh!
But amazingly, the small person evaded the attack with a nimble movement.
The startled Japanese man shouted.
“W-what the hell!”

The small person even ran along the flat of the katana and managed to drive their sword into the back of the Japanese man's hand—the first to do so. Their fighting prowess was truly remarkable. Startled, the Japanese man flung his arm out and shook them off.
“Damn it! That stings!”
Thrown aside, the small person screamed while tumbling across the plain.
The other Japanese man laughed with interest.
“······So one of them's pretty brave, huh?”
The attack had done virtually no damage, but the small person wore a faint smile after landing what was, for them, a satisfying blow.
A tiny scratch appeared on the back of the Japanese man's hand, as if he had been pricked by a needle.
“L-look! The disaster is bleeding!”
“Yaaaaay!”
A single drop of blood.
To the small people, it was a miraculous drop.
Even a disaster could be killed.
A god was a being that bled.
That single drop had taught them both.
“We can do it! Attack! Just a little more!”
Their morale rising, the small people stopped fleeing and began charging at the disasters instead.
“What's gotten into these things all of a sudden!”
“Get away! You fucking gnats!”
Clinging close, the small people swung swords smaller than toothpicks at the Japanese men's bodies.
Useless arrows dotted the air, and the cavalry refused to give up, holding formation as they thrust their lances at the Japanese men's feet.
They still did no damage, but the small people didn't give up.
Shin Yoosung watched with her fists clenched tight.
An indirect message came from somewhere.
[A constellation of the small planet is cheering on the incarnation ‘Gillemium.’]
Even this small planet had constellations, of course.
A constellation born on a small planet, nourished by the faith of small humans.
[A constellation of the small planet has sponsored the incarnation ‘Gillemium’ with 10 coins.]
The incarnation named ‘Gillemium’ seemed to be the small person who had first wounded the Japanese man.
“Kal—Saviooor!”
All the small people were excited, as if just a few more attacks would bring the enemy down.
That lasted precisely until the dokkaebi's voice rang out.
[What an interesting turn of events. Resistance does make a story more exciting, doesn't it?]
Ganul laughed, as if mocking the small people's resistance.
There was something familiar about that laugh.
[The greater the despair, the richer the story becomes.]
A pitch-black aura flowed from the bodies of the Japanese men under attack.
Realizing something was wrong, the small people abruptly stopped attacking and regrouped.
[Some ‘disaster’ penalties will now be lifted. Those who have chosen the ‘Path of Disaster’ may use additional buffs, so please be sure to check your Attributes Window.]
The Japanese men looked down at their bodies and snickered.
“What's this? You don't need to do this much for us.”
“There's a limit to how easy a game should be······. This just makes it even less fun.”
[It's all right for this one to be easy. Think of it as a game for relieving stress.]
“Well, if you insist······.”
Chuckling, the Japanese man readjusted his grip on his katana without hesitation.
Rooooar!
Powerful magic was gathering in their katanas.
Judging by the form of their stigmas, both Japanese men seemed to have samurai constellation sponsors.
They didn't seem to be famous ones, though······.
[Some of the disasters' probability restrictions have been lifted.]
[The disasters' maximum synchronization rate with their sponsors will increase for a limited time.]
[The Bureau of the <Star Stream> will pay the probability deficit on their behalf.]
Booooom!

The ground of the plain was crushed, and as many as a hundred small people split apart at once in fountains of blood. I wouldn't go so far as to call the destructive power terrifying, but it was certainly considerable. If even I saw it that way, then to those small people······.
······No, there were hardly any small people left to be shocked.

Faced with the overwhelming calamity, some small people wet and soiled themselves, while others simply fainted. Those who had been screaming frantically now stared blankly at the calamity, as if they had forgotten even how to scream.
“Ah, aah. Aaaah······.”
Dropping their weapons, the small people sank to their knees one by one.
Even the small person who had first wounded the Japanese man let a longsword fall to the ground. The courage that had filled the small people's eyes moments earlier was now utterly crushed.
「We can't win.」
「Our planet is now······.」
That despair took such a familiar form that merely reading it was painful.
[A constellation of the small planet has discovered you.]
Then a message reached me.
[A constellation of the small planet looks at you with pleading eyes.]
[A constellation of the small planet hopes for your sympathy toward the small planet.]
[A constellation of the small planet finds hope in you.]
[A constellation of the small planet has sponsored you with 10 coins.]
I frowned and looked up into the air.
[You have returned the 10 coins you received in sponsorship.]
Another message followed.
[A constellation of the small planet is flustered.]
[A constellation of the small planet blushes with shame.]
There seemed to be a misunderstanding.
The constellation probably thought I wouldn't act because 10 coins was too paltry a sum.
But that was wrong.
In a very quiet voice, I spoke into the air.
‘If you really care about your planet, don't do that shit.’
[A constellation of the small planet is flustered.]
‘Unless you want to turn your planet into a story bought and sold for money.’
[A constellation of the small planet falls silent in anguish.]
In the distance, the Japanese man's second strike was taking shape.
If it landed, the remaining small people would certainly be wiped out.
Shin Yoosung cried out.
“Ajusshi, I can't take any more.”
The black aura surrounding the Japanese men's bodies was gradually thinning.
The [Probability Buff] was slowly wearing off.
It was about time.
I spoke to Shin Yoosung.
“There's a way to clear the scenario without becoming a disaster.”
“······Ajusshi?”
“But it'll be really hard and horrible.”
Shin Yoosung's gaze wavered.
“You might want to give up. Can you still do it?”
In fact, this had been my plan from the start.
I had waited anyway to improve our chances of winning.
However pitiable this planet's inhabitants were, they were ultimately just ‘another species.’
And what mattered most right now were Shin Yoosung's life and mine.
[The disasters' probability restrictions are returning to their original state.]
The strength of the two samurai who had been wrapped in black auras was returning to normal. Shin Yoosung nodded.
“I can do it.”
At those words, I rushed forward.
[The <Star Stream> has detected signs of abnormality in you.]
[Warning. Take care not to act against your fellow disasters.]
Shin Yoosung would probably come to regret that decision. This scenario would show her exactly what happened to those who gave up the ‘ease’ of an easy scenario.
But sometimes, you had to give up ease to hold on to your convictions.
[Activating ‘Blade of Faith’!]
Light exploded, and a deafening roar shook the plain.
To put it bluntly, Peace Land's ‘small people’ were human, but they weren't ‘Earthlings’ like me.
However broadly I extended my love for humanity, there was a clear contradiction in opposing my fellow humans for a race from another planet.
So I wasn't acting out of some grand moral principle, such as doing it for ‘humanity’ or ‘justice.’
If I became an enemy of the ‘small people’ here, I would miss an achievement I needed for the ending.
That was my sole reason for driving the ‘Blade of Faith’ into the ground now.
BOOOOOM!
[The <Star Stream> has detected signs of abnormality in you.]
[Warning. Take care not to act against your fellow disasters.]
[If hostile acts continue to accumulate······.]
Thick clouds of dust rose, and the Japanese men screamed within them, their vision obscured.
“Aaaagh! What the hell was that?”
“Cough, cough!”
I had poured a considerable amount of magic power into the strike, so the dust wouldn't settle easily.
[The little heart of a constellation of the small planet is pounding.]
I considered it for a moment.
If I killed them with my own hands now, I could receive a new scenario immediately.
But the penalty I would receive for doing so would be indescribably horrible.
If possible, I wanted to put that moment off as long as I could.
So, at least······.
“Ajusshi, let me do it this time.”
Shin Yoosung drew the dagger Yoo Sangah had given her and stepped forward.
“I can take on both of them.”
“Can you do it?”
“No problem.”
Lee Gilyoung was the same. I didn't know why kids these days were so bold.
Yoo Sangah would have stopped her, of course, but I wasn't Yoo Sangah.
I spoke to encourage Shin Yoosung.
“You can't let the fight drag on. You heard the penalty message, right? You have to deal with them as quickly as possible.”
If Shin Yoosung could handle both of them, my options in this scenario would become considerably broader.
I had a lot to do in ‘Peace Land.’
One of my most important goals was to catch the ‘snake’ Persephone had mentioned.
If I could avoid getting penalized here beforehand, I might be able to catch the snake much sooner than I had expected.
“Which bastard did that!”
Shin Yoosung ran through the dust toward the voice.
Almost simultaneously, I concealed myself with the [Hermit's Cloak].
The item would be useless against an advanced detection skill, but I doubted those samurai had one.
Swoooosh!
Sharp magic power rippled from Shin Yoosung's dagger, tracing a menacing crescent.
“Aaaagh!”
The Japanese men recoiled from the strike that flew out of the dust.
A strike that had deliberately missed.
She had let a perfect opportunity slip, but if she could drive them off without a fight, that would be one way to do it.
Startled by the surprise attack, the Japanese men looked puzzled when a child emerged from the dust.
“What the hell? It's just a kid.”
After murmuring to each other, they questioned Shin Yoosung.
“Hey, kid. Why are you stopping us?”
“Don't you know what happens if you do that?”
Unfortunately, unlike me, Shin Yoosung didn't have the [Interpreter] skill, so their words were just a foreign language to her.
“······What are they saying?”
Only then did the Japanese men catch on.
“Could she be a Korean participant?”
“Oh, right! I heard Korea's first wave just entered too······.”
“Damn it, if she's from the first wave, she'll be really strong······.”
Their faces darkened rapidly.
“Get out of the way, kid. We don't need to fight each other.”
“Don't fight! Don't fight! Okay?”
“We just need to kill them. Small people. Kill! Okay?”
The Japanese men used clumsy English to make it clear they didn't want to fight, but Shin Yoosung simply shook her head. When her sharp dagger pointed at them, their shoulders jerked.
“Die or fuck off. Those are your only choices.”
As Shin Yoosung approached, the Japanese men began edging backward.
“Damn it······ I can't. I'm in the middle of a bounty scenario.”
“······My sponsor's telling me to just kill the little brat.”
“There are two of us. Couldn't we manage it?”
“Have you forgotten how strong our first-wave guys were?”
They were fairly smart.

Everywhere in the world, each country's finest elites were selected for the first wave of the sixth scenario. Japan probably had a considerable gap between its first wave and the later ones too. Similar feelings were surfacing on both Japanese men's faces.
「······Should we run?」
Meanwhile, a strange joy was spreading among the small people watching Shin Yoosung confront the Japanese men.
“What on earth······?”
Their surprise was understandable.
A small disaster had suddenly appeared and was fighting larger disasters.
“Could it be the ‘Small Savior’······!”
“The p-prophecy was right!”
[A constellation of the small planet is moved by the incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung.’]
[A constellation of the small planet has sponsored the incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ with 10 coins.]
[The incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ has obtained the possibility of a new scenario.]
Watching the scene, I tightened and loosened my grip on my sword hilt.
It left me a little uneasy, but driving them off and then tracking their movements was one option.
But if my thinking was right, things wouldn't go so smoothly.
The intermediate dokkaebi Ganul drifted in the air, watching with interest, then snickered.
[You Japanese participants seem to think you're at a disadvantage. But are you really?]
That fucking dokkaebi bastard.
The Japanese men muttered as something dawned on them.
“Oh, right! Come to think of it, among the first-wave participants······.”
“They said Asuka transformed after doing this too, didn't they? I guess Korea would have oddballs like that as well. If we tell her now······.”
“No need to tell her. She's just a Chōsenjin brat anyway.”
Once the Japanese men had made their decision, the look in their eyes changed.
Both murderous gazes turned toward Shin Yoosung at once.
“All right, let's fight.”
“I'm not into little kids, but······.”

Even without understanding their words, Shin Yoosung quickly grasped the situation from their unpleasant laughter. Their blades slid into motion, and the two men slowly surrounded her from front and back.
A keen killing intent seemed to rise from all three of them, and the two men moved their blades in unison.
Swoooosh!
Having raised her Agility to the maximum, Shin Yoosung dodged the blades without difficulty, but by a narrower margin than I had expected.
They might not measure up to the elites sent in with the first wave, but judging by their fighting skills, they seemed to rank fairly high among Japan's incarnations.
Watching their swordsmanship, I recalled the descriptions in ‘Ways of Survival.’
They were each using only one sword, so it wasn't Niten Ichi-ryu (二天一流), and judging by the blades' length, it wasn't Ganryu (岩流) either.
In other words, I didn't have to worry about any connection to Japan's greatest swordsmen, Miyamoto Musashi or Sasaki Kojiro.
Not bad opponents for Shin Yoosung's debut fight.
“It'll be hard to keep running away, kid!”

As their sponsors imbued their sword techniques with keen energy, the blades grew even more menacing. A blade that seemed to be cutting at her leg aimed for her waist; one that seemed to be aiming at her arm went for her neck. Seamless feints threaded through every part of their attacks.
Before long, Shin Yoosung's movements were caught in the shadows of their blades.
However high her overall stats were, they held an overwhelming advantage in practiced swordsmanship.
Swish!
Shin Yoosung's collar was slashed, and a fine line appeared on her arm.
I gripped my sword hilt firmly, ready to move at any moment.
I was supposed to be her sponsor, yet I couldn't give her even one decent stigma. It was frustrating.
“Diiie!”
With the exaggerated cries characteristic of the Japanese, the two katanas crossed, each targeting a different part of Shin Yoosung's body. This time, she didn't dodge.
Claaang!
Her Strength inferior to theirs, Shin Yoosung lost her dagger, and a katana seized the opportunity to slip through the opening. But she didn't panic.
[The character ‘Shin Yoosung’ has activated ‘Advanced Diverse Communication Lv.3.’]
Instead, she sprang backward, somersaulted in the air, and landed on the back of a waiting monster. It was the Steel Wolf she had tamed earlier.
“······What the hell?”
The right decision.
The basic principle of combat was to minimize your opponent's strengths and maximize your own.
Awoooo!
With the wolf's howl, dozens of Steel Wolves burst out of the forest at once.
She had tamed that many wolves in such a short time.
That was the potential of the future ‘Beast Lord,’ all right.
“What the fuck?”
The startled men swung their swords to fend off the wolves, but the wolves that had already lunged at them clamped onto their arms and legs.
“Fuck! You sons of bitches!”
Weakened or not, Grade-7 monsters would be difficult for men who had already used up a considerable amount of magic power to handle.
It really was a sight that made teaching her worthwhile.
But Shin Yoosung still didn't know.
Why I had told her ‘not to drag it out.’
[The <Star Stream> has detected abnormal behavior from the incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung.’]
[Hostile action against fellow disasters has been detected.]
[The incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ will receive the first scenario penalty.]
The penalties had finally begun.
Feeling her magic power suddenly diminish, Shin Yoosung let out a groan.
Some of the wolves abruptly broke free of her control and returned to the forest.
[The body volume of the character ‘Shin Yoosung’ has decreased.]
[The overall stats of the character ‘Shin Yoosung’ have decreased.]
Noticing the change, the Japanese men shouted.
“Y-yes! I knew this would happen!”
“We just have to hold out a little longer!”
······So it came to this after all.
I could feel Shin Yoosung searching for me with anxious eyes.
Still wearing the [Hermit's Cloak], I approached her from behind and placed a hand on her shoulder.
Her trembling shoulders settled again.
“······Thank you, ajusshi.”
Having come to some understanding on her own, Shin Yoosung bit her lip.
[The incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ will receive the second scenario penalty.]
Shin Yoosung's body was growing smaller and smaller.
That was the result of a ‘disaster’ voluntarily relinquishing her own authority.
But she still had enough strength left to take the Japanese men's lives.
Using her Agility to its fullest, Shin Yoosung approached the men from behind like a wild beast.
“U-uaaagh!”
Had she picked that up from watching Yoo Sangah at some point?
Once she hardened her heart, Shin Yoosung's dagger skills were truly outstanding.
The dagger moved, and the man's carotid artery helplessly spewed blood.
Pssshhh.
“G-guhhh, th-this can't······.”
The stream of blood pattered onto the plain as the man's pallid face drew closer to the ground.
[The character ‘Shin Yoosung’ has defeated a ‘Disaster Without a Name Yet.’]
[Major Contributor : Shin Yoosung]
Wiping the blood spattered on her cheek, Shin Yoosung moved toward her next target.
The terrified man crawled backward. Steel Wolves rushed at him, tearing savagely at his arms and legs.
“G-gaaaaaagh!”
Shin Yoosung approached to finish him off.
That was when the unexpected happened.
[The incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ has been completely stripped of her rights as a ‘disaster.’]
[The dokkaebis of the <Star Stream> have deemed the actions of ‘Shin Yoosung’ acts of opposition to the scenario.]
[The incarnation ‘Shin Yoosung’ will receive the third scenario penalty.]
[Miniaturization (小人化) will begin.]
In this scenario, anyone who relinquished their standing as a predator would come to resemble the prey they had hunted.
Crrrrrack.
Shin Yoosung's body began shrinking far faster than it had before.
With a faint groan, the clothes Shin Yoosung wore rapidly grew larger, and the dagger in her hand fell to the ground.
Shin Yoosung, who had reached my waist, shrank to knee height, then from my knees to my shins, until her body disappeared beneath her clothes.
As her stats dropped and her control weakened, all the Steel Wolves returned to the forest.
A tiny Shin Yoosung crawled out of her clothes and limped toward the man.
“Yoosung, you can stop now.”
Panting, Shin Yoosung turned to look at me.
Fierce resolve and sorrow mingled in the child's reddened eyes.
She had plenty of experience fighting monsters, but this was probably the first time she had committed such a deliberate act of murder.
“He's already unconscious.”
At my words, Shin Yoosung looked toward the fallen Japanese man.
He lay sprawled on the ground, foaming at the mouth.
I tore a little fabric from her discarded clothes and covered her body.
Now as small as my fist, Shin Yoosung looked over her body a few times, then clenched and unclenched her hands.
She was probably coming to understand what had happened to her.
“Do I have to fight people like them in this state?”
“Yes.”
“······How many are left?”
“Quite a lot.”
Shin Yoosung looked up at me with troubled eyes.
“You knew, didn't you, ajusshi? That opposing the disasters would turn us into small people.”
I nodded and approached the fallen Japanese man.
On closer inspection, he was a young man in his early twenties at most.
He was still breathing.
“Are you going to use him?”
“There's someone I have to kill before I transform.”
As soon as I said that, new messages rang out.
[Take care not to act against your fellow disasters.]
[A disaster that acts against another disaster will lose all rights as a ‘disaster.’]
The dokkaebi still floated in the sky, looking utterly delighted.
All right······.
Let's see how long you can keep laughing like that.
[The <Star Stream> considers your ‘disaster activities’ insufficient.]
[If you do not kill a member of Peace Land's dominant species within the next hour, you will be deemed unwilling to act as a disaster and stripped of your ‘disaster’ status.]
Looking down at the Japanese man foaming at the mouth, I slowly took off my cloak.
I had one hour left now.
Within that hour, I had to take down their ‘king.’
「As he walked through the forest, Suzuki kept thinking.
‘I was really lucky.’

Suzuki shuddered as he recalled what had just happened. A girl who controlled monsters and wielded a dagger with considerable skill. He probably wouldn't be able to forget how his companion Murakami had died in a single blow for quite some time.
‘Korea is frightening. Even a child is already at that level.’

If the child was that strong, Suzuki could hardly guess how skilled the man beside him was. A man in a snow-white coat, with a white sword at his side. Apart from the color of his coat, there was nothing particularly special about his attire, but in any case, he had saved Suzuki's life.
“Thank you so much for earlier. Without you, I would have died there.”
“Don't mention it.”
“Honestly, I was touched. I never expected to receive help from a Korean.”
“We help each other get by.”
The man in the white coat was modest.
Above all, Suzuki liked that he spoke Japanese well.
It was undoubtedly thanks to a skill, but possessing a Japanese interpretation skill was presumably evidence of his usual fondness for Japanese culture.
“Oh, we haven't introduced ourselves yet. What did you say your name was? I'm Suzuki Tatsuya.”
“I'm Dokja. Kim Dokja.”
“Kimu-Dogeza?”
“······Kim Dokja.”
“Oh.”
Kim Dogeza.
Wasn't that an exceedingly polite name?
Suzuki liked this Korean's name.
“But did you see that child? The one who killed my companion······.”
“Unfortunately, I lost her.”
“Whew······ I see.”
He couldn't tell whether it was true.
He also thought there was nothing he could do even if it wasn't.
This man was Korean too, after all.
It wouldn't be strange if he had hidden the child or pretended not to see her.
Still, a disappointment was a disappointment.
If he could just catch her, revenge would have been so easy.
As a member of Japan's third wave, he already knew about ‘Miniaturization,’ the hidden piece of the ‘sixth scenario.’
“Since you saved me, Kim-san, you must have witnessed ‘Miniaturization’ too.”
“If you mean her body getting smaller, yes, of course I saw it.”
“Then that makes things simple. We may be from different countries, but there's no need for us to oppose each other in this scenario. Our enemies are the ‘small people,’ not our fellow humans.”
“I know. That's why I saved you, Suzuki-ssi.”
Fortunately, the Korean before him seemed to agree with his views.
Kim Dogeza spoke.
“By the way, it seems the Japanese side already knew quite a few things.”
“Yes. We progressed through the scenarios quickly, and there were a few similar cases among the earlier participants.”
“Similar cases?”
“There were a few Earthlings who turned into small people.”
“What happened to them?”
“Most died, and one is still alive.”
Hearing that, Kim Dogeza seemed to be thinking about something.
A Korean whose thoughts were difficult to fathom.
Growing a little uneasy, Suzuki spoke.
“Let me say in advance that I don't dislike Korea.”
“······Why would you say that?”
“Don't Koreans think all Japanese people dislike Korea?”
That was something the ‘Prime Minister,’ one of Japan's first-wave participants, had said.
Of course, he wasn't the actual prime minister. It was a nickname.
―Koreans still have a strong sense of nationalism. When someone insults their country, they think they're being insulted personally.
Suzuki didn't like the Prime Minister, but listening to him had never done him any harm.
“Kim-san. I like both Kim Ayeon and Park Seongji.”
“I really enjoyed Autumn Sonata too. My mother also likes it.”
When you meet a Korean, mention Kim Ayeon, Park Seongji, and Autumn Sonata.
That had been the Prime Minister's advice.
“I like Japanese manga too.”
“O-oh! I thought you might.”
The Prime Minister really did seem to have been right.
Needlessly excited, Suzuki asked.
“What manga do you like?”
“It's hard to choose just one. Besides, I don't even know whether I'll be able to keep reading them now.”
“······Yes, that is a shame. There was a manga I looked forward to every week, but now I don't even know whether the artist is alive.”
Thinking about things like that left a bitter taste.
Suzuki had things he loved too.
Manga was one of them.
“Everything has changed, after all.”」
―Ajusshi.
Shin Yoosung's voice broke my immersion.
I had been using Stage 2 of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint to its fullest, so I couldn't answer her immediately.

Somehow stall for time and flee back into the forest labyrinth, or else······.

······I probably wouldn't die here, but one wrong move could leave me seriously injured.

Ratatatatat!

Well, now.

What looked like a good hundred or so turrets fired simultaneously, and the Japanese screamed in pain.

Ratatatatat!
Thin trickles of blood ran from bullet wounds all over the Japanese men's bodies.
“My eye! My eye!”
“What is this?! What the hell is this?!”
Shells came flying from every angle, forming a web of fire. Hit in their vital spots, the Japanese screamed and collapsed.

The Armed Fortress Master, all right.

“F-fall back! Retreat for now!”

Rrrrrrumble.

“Waaaaaah!”

······That voice?

······Goddess-nim?

Her short dress fluttered in the wind as she landed on the ground with a soft thud.
That familiar arrogant gaze and haughty expression.
She really hadn't changed at all.

“Well, haven't you come up in the world?”

“You seem to have forgotten where we are.”

How the hell were those dokkaebi bastards doing their jobs?

Han Sooyoung brushed off her skirt and grumbled.
“Honestly, I go to the trouble of saving you, and all you do is complain.”
“What is it? Tell me.”
“Have you already forgotten who I am?”
“Huh?”
“Did your brain shrink too, just because your head got smaller?”

Han Sooyoung was now the only ‘Prophet’ left in the Seoul Dome.

Given 3 weeks and knowledge of the future, even if that Han Sooyoung had suddenly become the goddess of an unfamiliar world······ No, something still felt a little strange.
A queen, I could understand, but a goddess?
“You two little shits sure are in sync.”
At the voice, I turned to see Gong Pildu beside us, looking displeased.

“Gong Pildu.”
“What?”
“Sorry.”

Who was really in sync here?

“Then do better next time.”

Anyway, I was glad they were both alive, even if they'd become small.

Neither of them was the sort to do that, were they?

“Oh, no. I just did what needed to be done.”

“She's just an old friend.”

I didn't have any friends anyway.
I couldn't see Han Sooyoung's face with her head lowered.
“Um, I'm sorry to interrupt, but······ may I ask something?”

Lee Jihye chimed in too.
“······Come to think of it, who's that Japanese woman? Is she a friend too?”

That damn brat.

“Who is she? Was there someone like her in the original?”

“Um, my question······.”

“How have you already taken control of the northern region of [Peace Land]?”
I see.

The kingdom of Veronica, falling to ruin under the disasters.

People grown gaunt in the face of overwhelming calamity.
